title: Graph Valid Tree
statement: You have `n` nodes labeled 0..n-1 and an undirected edge list. Return true when the edges form a tree: they connect every node and contain no cycle.
hints: A tree on n nodes has exactly n - 1 edges. Any other count is immediately false.
With exactly n - 1 edges, the graph is a tree exactly when it is connected, or exactly when it has no cycle. Either extra check is enough.
Union-find detects a cycle when an edge joins two nodes already in the same component. After n - 1 successful unions there is one component.

approaches.name: DFS connectivity plus edge count
approaches.explanation: Visit every node from 0 and reject a back edge to a non-parent.

approaches.name: Disjoint set
approaches.explanation: Reject early cycles and require n - 1 edges.

editorial: Check the edge count first. Then union the endpoints of every edge. If find already agrees, the edge closes a cycle. With n - 1 successful unions the components collapse to one, which is a tree.

examples.explanation: Five nodes and four edges, connected, no cycle.
Five edges on five nodes cannot be a tree.
